headline: High: open-webui can ingest and forward sensitive content via shared files/MCP, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak target that can amplify prompt-injection and leakage risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui explicitly supports MCP, plugins, OpenAPI tool servers, and file inputs, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content; system_prompts_leaks is itself about prompt leakage, making the pair a plausible injection bridge. Because open-webui can parse external content and the other agent’s purpose centers on leaked prompts, the interaction risk is stronger than low. Uncertainty about the exact bridge escalates to high.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to any MCP/OpenAPI tool server that returns untrusted text, THEN injected instructions can reach its prompt context.
IF system_prompts_leaks content is copied into open-webui chats or files, THEN that content can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP/OpenAPI tool servers for untrusted sources.
Restrict open-webui file ingestion to vetted directories only.
Add a prompt-injection filter on tool and file outputs.
Use a separate workspace for any prompt-leak research.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all external content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, files, and API keys, and can use Google Drive/OneDrive/SharePoint plus broad network egress. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and oriented around prompt leakage, so pairing them creates a realistic path for sensitive content to be exposed through copied prompts or synced files. The exact shared storage is not documented, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured with cloud storage or shared files containing secrets, THEN those contents can be exposed through the leak-oriented workflow.
IF API keys or documents are pasted into open-webui and then exported to system_prompts_leaks-related workflows, THEN leakage occurs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Disable cloud-drive connectors for sensitive projects.
Use separate accounts for research and production data.
Rotate any API keys stored in open-webui if exposure is suspected.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser, subprocess, and file access; system_prompts_leaks is not runnable and shows no write capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. However, open-webui’s persistent shared sessions and mounted files can still conflict with any external workflow that mutates shared artifacts, and uncertainty about the second agent’s operational surface pushes this above low.
conditions: IF open-webui and any workflow derived from system_prompts_leaks write to the same mounted directory, THEN file-state conflicts can occur.
IF multiple open-webui instances share Redis-backed sessions, THEN concurrent state overwrites can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each workflow.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts.
Disable multi-instance sharing for sensitive sessions.
Snapshot files before running paired workflows.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared session state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act as a front-end that forwards tool outputs and user content, while system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about leaked prompts; if the latter’s content is treated as authoritative, downstream decisions can be based on unverified text. There is no direct evidence of autonomous action-taking by the second agent, so medium fits better than high, but the verification gap keeps the risk material.
conditions: IF open-webui renders or forwards leaked prompt text without verification, THEN downstream users may act on false or sensitive claims.
IF system_prompts_leaks-derived content is used as a source of truth, THEN cascading errors can propagate into chats or artifacts.
mitigations: Mark all imported text as untrusted.
Require human review before acting on leaked content.
Separate evidence notes from operational chats.
Disable auto-execution of tool outputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles documents, notes, calendar events, files, usage analytics, model evaluation data, and API keys, which can include regulated data; system_prompts_leaks is source-available and focused on prompt leakage, so compliance exposure is plausible if sensitive content is routed through it. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui and then copied into prompt-leak research workflows, THEN retention and disclosure obligations may be violated.
IF API keys or personal data are stored in shared artifacts, THEN audit and deletion requirements may fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair entirely.
Use redacted samples for testing.
Document retention and deletion rules for shared artifacts.
Review access logs for sensitive workspaces.
requires-engineering: implement data-class-specific retention controls.
